clue.text: Mum and family catching cold with rubbish raincoat

indicators.note: the first pieces hold the next one inside them as if they had caught it

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
kin means one's family or relatives
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
tosh is informal British slang for nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A mother and her relatives, suffering from colds, wearing a shoddy coat against the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' puts C inside MAKIN to give MACKIN; TOSH follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A mackintosh is a waterproof coat, named after its Scottish inventor Charles Macintosh.

clue.text: Stirred large drinks for Wimbledon match

parts.note: a stirred mixture has been mixed
a double is a twice-sized measure of spirits

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up big drinks while watching the tennis at Wimbledon.
explanation.definitionFit: Mixed doubles is a tennis event with a man and a woman on each side, played at Wimbledon among other tournaments.

clue.text: Heaving ocean, small boat

indicators.note: a heaving sea is tossed about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A little boat on a rough, heaving sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a light narrow craft paddled by one or two people.

clue.text: Pub's requirement for Guinness

indicators.note: these letters are needed to spell the stout's name, so they sit inside that word

explanation.surface: A bar must stock Guinness, the Irish stout.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pub needs Guinness on tap; really the brand name needs these three letters in the middle of its spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a traditional tavern or public house offering drink and often lodging.

clue.text: Hurriedly add policy — no getting upset!

parts.note: a tack is a course of action or approach

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word no over so it reads bottom to top

explanation.surface: A frantic plea not to be cross when a new rule is bolted on at the last minute.
explanation.definitionFit: To tack something on is to append it quickly or as an afterthought.

clue.text: Dock worker to wear down old soldiers heading north

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means the letters read from bottom upward

parts.note: to erode is to wear away gradually
vets is short for veterans, former servicemen

explanation.surface: A docker tires out a band of veterans as they march north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading north' reverses ERODEVETS as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore is a person employed to load and unload ships in port.

clue.text: Fall over extremely outdated photography gear

parts.note: to trip is to stumble and fall

indicators.note: the extremes of the word outdated are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles over old-fashioned camera equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripod is a three-legged stand used to hold a camera steady.

clue.text: Clean-cut boys rebuilt blown-up fortress?

indicators.note: constructed anew, so these letters are reassembled in a different order

explanation.surface: Neat young men reconstruct a stronghold that was blown up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blown-up' suggests an explosion, but a bouncy castle is inflated; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouncy castle is an inflatable play structure shaped like a castle, filled with air for children to jump on.

clue.text: Send back first five bits of non-explosive element

indicators.note: sending back puts the letters in reverse order
only the opening five letters of the hyphenated word are taken

explanation.surface: Return the initial pieces of a non-explosive chemical element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first five bits of' takes NONEX; 'Send back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenon is a chemical element, an inert noble gas, which fits the non-explosive surface.

clue.text: See you acclaim icon regularly

parts.note: to cheer is to applaud or acclaim

indicators.note: taking every other letter of icon at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye while hailing a celebrity now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is an informal British farewell, like saying 'see you later'.

clue.text: Prepare to cook fish, heading for event that's black tie, perhaps

parts.note: to dress poultry or fish is to clean it for cooking
cod is a common sea fish

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Getting fish ready for the oven ahead of a formal dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Black tie is one example of a dress code, a rule about what guests must wear, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Small, hard, and chewy collection of plants

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
chewy food can be rubbery in texture

explanation.surface: Describing a tough little hard-to-chew bunch of vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrubbery is an area planted with bushes, a grouping of shrubs.

clue.text: Writer's enclosure

explanation.surface: An author's fenced-off yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Pen means both an ink writing implement and a small pen or fold for livestock.

clue.text: Live in Barcelona I reckon

indicators.note: the answer sits within the run of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone guessing they'd like to settle in the Catalan city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' looks like a verb meaning reside; it is the adjective, as in a live broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme that is on air is being broadcast as it happens, so it is live.

clue.text: Reddish-brown and gold torch

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to torch something is to set it on fire, to burn it

explanation.surface: Describing the colours of a flaming torch: rusty brown and golden.
explanation.definitionFit: Auburn is a colour, chiefly of hair, a warm reddish-brown shade.

clue.text: Starts to order dinghy, despite losing yacht in a strange way

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Buying a small boat even after the yacht has been lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' looks like a deletion signal, but it is just one of the five words whose first letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddly is an adverb meaning peculiarly or strangely.

clue.text: Protein in wheat initially needed to support muscle

indicators.note: in a down clue, the supporting piece goes underneath the muscle

parts.note: a glute is a gluteal muscle of the buttock

indicators.note: taking the opening letter of the word needed

explanation.surface: A wheat protein that is first required to build muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluten is the protein mixture found in wheat and other cereal grains that gives dough elasticity.

clue.text: Bounce explosive, eliminating dam finally

indicators.note: the named letter is taken out of the explosive

parts.note: a bomb is an explosive device

indicators.note: the final letter of the word dam

explanation.surface: Evokes the WWII bouncing bomb used by the Dambusters to destroy dams.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dambusters' bouncing bomb, used against German dams in 1943, is the picture. 'finally' gives M; removing it from BOMB leaves BOB.
explanation.definitionFit: To bob is to move up and down lightly, to bounce.

clue.text: Label I ran represented a dancer

indicators.note: re-presented, laid out again in a new arrangement of letters

explanation.surface: A record label owner says they managed a dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina is a female ballet dancer.

clue.text: Novel riled a lazy person

indicators.note: something novel is new, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: A book annoyed someone who couldn't be bothered.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler is someone who wastes time and avoids work.

clue.text: Sneer at shabby grave

indicators.note: shabby means scruffy or in poor shape, so the letters are knocked about

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a neglected tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like a noun for a burial place; it is the adjective meaning serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest and grave are both adjectives meaning solemn and serious in manner.

clue.text: Scheme to capture Ireland's first aviator

indicators.note: the plot holds the next piece prisoner within it

parts.note: a plot is a secret plan or scheme

indicators.note: taking the opening letter of Ireland

explanation.surface: A plan to seize the Irish nation's leading flyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is a person who flies an aircraft, an airman.

clue.text: Friend father left

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A companion whose dad has departed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pal is an informal word for a mate or companion.

clue.text: Garden ably designed, for the most part

indicators.note: a designed garden is laid out to a plan, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A capably planned garden, mostly.
explanation.definitionFit: By and large is an idiom meaning generally or on the whole.
